routes.note: The preformal goal version is superseded by the completed formal statement and its real compiler certificate. This is not a failed mathematical route.

C9000181.statement: Adversarially audit, verify, or refute OpenAI Manuscript Family 181 (The Erdős–Gallai cycle-decomposition conjecture.; papers: A linear cycle-and-edge decomposition of every graph; Lean status: Partially/Comparator formalized (lean/docs/181.md)): either (a) discover and certify an explicit mathematical flaw, sign/orientation error, counterexample to an intermediate lemma, or statement-fidelity/citation gap with a deterministic symbolic/computational certificate (`verify.py` + `exact_certificate.json`), or (b) independently verify, repair, or generalize the manuscript's core mathematical theorem with a standalone machine-checkable certificate certified by the independent Reviewer.

M_MAIN.statement: Every finite simple graph on n vertices has an edge partition into at most Cn simple cycles and single edges for an absolute C.

M_INDUCTION.statement: The scale-prefix induction pays for all decomposed edges and recursive graph orders.

M_SCALE_SPLIT.statement: The scale-splitting lemma gives expanding pieces and sparse residual boxes with the claimed order-sum control.

M_SMALL_RESIDUE.statement: The small-residue construction decomposes an expanding piece with the claimed residue-order savings.

M_SAMPLING.statement: Edge splitting and vertex sampling retain the expansion and concentration budgets required by small residue.

M_BATCH_RESOLUTION.statement: Pair folding, simplification, and simple-cycle lifting meet the batch-resolution cost bounds.

M_PAIR_FOLDING.statement: The pair-folding construction preserves representative-edge assignments with only the stated linear errors.

D_TEAM_ROUTING.statement: The root theorem and the bounded-rank matching theorem imply the manuscript's indexed-team routing conclusion, including endpoint exceptions.

A_MATCHING.statement: Bucic--Montgomery arXiv:2211.07689v2 Theorem 6 supplies disjoint representatives under the stated bounded-rank matching condition.

V_ROUTING_BUDGET.statement: The manuscript's obstruction, endpoint-load, and expansion inequalities imply all three budgets of the root theorem.

V_ROUTING_ROOT.statement: For arbitrary root-specific forbidden sets and the stated common-edge budgets, some root ball exceeds r/2 by radius ceil(8(r/h)log_2(2r))(1+ceil(log_2|S|)).
V_ROUTING_ROOT.note: Kernel-verified universal graph theorem; open here only pending independent statement-fidelity and scope review.

V_UNION_GROWTH.statement: Actual unions of labelled graph balls grow by a factor at least 1+h/(2r) under the local deletion threshold.
V_UNION_GROWTH.note: Derived from actual graph boundary edges in the compiled file; independent review pending.

V_GROWTH_BLOCK.statement: The derived graph-growth inequality forces a union above r/2 within the ceiling-defined growth block.
V_GROWTH_BLOCK.note: The ceiling-defined growth block is proved in the compiled file; independent review pending.

V_ROOT_HALVING.statement: A large labelled union can be reduced to a singleton using at most ceil(log_2|S|) root halvings, with one growth block per halving.
V_ROOT_HALVING.note: Label-preserving root halving is proved in the compiled file; independent review pending.
